subject.title: [security] Portal cookies lack host-prefix protection against sibling-origin shadowing

question: Should Crabbox change the portal and isolated Code viewer cookies to __Host- names, including the Code viewer Path=/ transition and legacy-cookie clearing behavior?
rationale: The issue affects the portal authentication/session boundary, and the Code viewer cookie transition changes browser cookie scope semantics that should be explicitly accepted by the security owner.

options.title: Land host-prefixed cookie transition
options.body: Rename both managed browser session cookies to __Host- names, clear the legacy names during transition, and test duplicate-cookie shadowing no longer selects attacker-controlled legacy cookies.

options.title: Reject duplicates without renaming
options.body: Keep the public cookie names but reject ambiguous duplicate Cookie headers, which reduces parser confusion but does not get browser-enforced host-only protection.

options.title: Accept current deployment risk
options.body: Document that deployments sharing lower-trust sibling origins must avoid parent-domain cookie control, leaving the current cookie names unchanged.

recommendation.title: Land host-prefixed cookie transition
recommendation.body: Rename both managed browser session cookies to __Host- names, clear the legacy names during transition, and test duplicate-cookie shadowing no longer selects attacker-controlled legacy cookies.

likelyOwner.reason: This login has the clearest history on the portal authentication and browser Code session boundary touched by the decision.
